holidays.name: National Blueberry Pancake Day
holidays.description: A day to stack up fluffy pancakes studded with juicy blueberries, drown them in syrup, and call it a perfectly reasonable breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
holidays.origin: Like many American food days, it is an unofficial observance that grew out of food marketing and social media calendars. Blueberries became a pancake staple in the United States, where wild blueberries are native to North America.
holidays.funFact: Blueberries were one of the few fruits native to North America that Indigenous peoples used extensively, and the Wild Blueberry is Maine's official state berry.

holidays.name: Data Privacy Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to reminding everyone to stop using 'password123', read those terms and conditions at least once, and protect personal information online.
holidays.origin: It began in Europe as Data Protection Day in 2007 to mark the anniversary of Convention 108, signed on January 28, 1981, the first legally binding international treaty on data protection. North America adopted Data Privacy Day in 2008.
holidays.funFact: Convention 108 was signed in 1981, before the public internet existed, which makes the treaty surprisingly ahead of its time.

holidays.name: National Kazoo Day
holidays.description: A buzzing, humming celebration of the humble kazoo, the only instrument where you can sound like a bumblebee with a record deal.
holidays.origin: An informal fun observance honoring the kazoo, a membranophone that is said to have been popularized in the United States in the 1850s. The modern metal kazoo is often tied to Georgia and later to a factory in Eden, New York.
holidays.funFact: The kazoo does not work by blowing air through it like a flute. You have to hum or sing into it, and the vibrating membrane changes your voice.

holidays.name: National Fun at Work Day
holidays.description: A day when employees are encouraged to lighten up, play office games, and remember that spreadsheets are only slightly less fun when you wear a silly hat.
holidays.origin: Promoted by workplace culture and team-building advocates as an unofficial observance meant to boost morale and reduce workplace stress. It is also observed in some years as an excuse to do something silly in the break room.
holidays.funFact: Studies on workplace happiness have repeatedly linked employee enjoyment with higher productivity, so laughing at work can be a legit strategy.

holidays.name: Lego Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the iconic interlocking plastic bricks that have caused millions of people to step on them barefoot and still love them anyway.
holidays.origin: Lego Day marks the anniversary of the patent for the modern Lego brick, filed in Denmark on January 28, 1958 by Godtfred Kirk Christiansen.
holidays.funFact: Lego bricks made today still fit with bricks made in 1958, which is why the toy is famous for its remarkable compatibility across the decades.
